common_name: Claridge Druce Cranesbill (Vigorous Self-Seeding Pink Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Claridge Druce is one of the toughest and most vigorous hardy geraniums, tolerating dry shade and neglect while spreading steadily by both rhizome and self-sown seedlings.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this naturally occurring hybrid forms a sprawling, wide-spreading clump of semi-evergreen foliage covered from late spring through summer in deep rosy-pink flowers netted with darker veins. It is exceptionally vigorous and tolerant of dry shade, poor soil, and root competition under trees, making it one of the most reliable large-scale groundcovers among cranesbills, though its willingness to self-sow means deadheading spent flowers helps keep it from wandering beyond its allotted space. Shear the mounded foliage back hard after the first flush of bloom to tidy the plant and encourage a second round of flowers into fall.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Wargrave Pink is an old, dependable selection that tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil better than many hardy geraniums once established.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Wargrave Pink produces a long, generous display of salmon-pink flowers with faintly darker veining from late spring well into autumn, longer than most hardy geraniums manage without deadheading. It forms a mounded, mildew-resistant clump of lobed foliage that stays presentable through the heat of summer and tolerates considerably more drought and poor soil than its refined flower color might suggest. Cutting the plant back partway after the first big flush encourages fresh foliage and continued bloom, and established clumps can be divided every three to four years to renew vigor.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Buxton's Blue scrambles outward through the season and benefits from nearby shrubs or perennials to lean on.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, keeping the roots reliably cool and moist through summer for the best flowering. Buxton's Blue is prized for its unusually long season of bloom, opening large, clear sky-blue flowers with a small white eye continuously from midsummer until hard frost, later into the season than most other cranesbills. Its loosely sprawling, semi-trailing stems weave attractively through neighboring perennials or spill over a border edge rather than forming a tight mound, and light trimming in midseason keeps growth from becoming too lax. It is less drought-tolerant than many hardy geraniums and appreciates supplemental water during dry spells.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Bevan's Variety Bigroot Geranium (Deep Magenta-Pink Groundcover Cranesbill)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in well-drained, average to poor soil in partial shade to full sun in spring; like the species, Bevan's Variety spreads by surface rhizomes and tolerates dry shade under mature trees better than almost any other flowering groundcover.

directions: Plant divisions in well-drained, average to poor soil in partial to full shade; Bevan's Variety is a deeper-colored selection of bigroot geranium, bearing rich magenta-pink flowers on red-tinged stems above the same aromatic, lobed, dry-shade-tolerant foliage as the species. The stronger flower color makes it stand out against the softer pink and white forms typically sold, while retaining all of the parent plant's toughness under the dry shade of mature trees and shrubs where little else thrives. Sticky, scented leaves resist deer and rabbit browsing and take on attractive red and orange tones in fall. Divide congested patches in spring or fall to control spread or start new plantings elsewhere.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Gravetye is a more vigorous, larger-flowered selection of Himalayan geranium named after William Robinson's famous Gravetye Manor garden.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers run hot. Gravetye produces noticeably larger violet-blue, dark-veined flowers than the species type over a longer period in late spring and early summer, held above a loose mound of deeply lobed, softly hairy foliage that spreads gently by rhizome without becoming aggressive. Its rich blue tone pairs especially well with pink- and apricot-flowered border companions, and cutting the clump back hard after the main bloom flush tidies the foliage and can prompt a lighter rebloom later in the season. Divide every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Kashmir White spreads by creeping rhizomes to form a loose colony and benefits from a spring or fall division every few years to keep it from thinning in the center.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Kashmir White bears crisp white flowers finely traced with pale lilac-purple veins over deeply cut, ferny foliage from late spring into midsummer. Native to the Kashmir region of the western Himalayas, it spreads steadily by creeping rhizomes to form a loose, weaving patch that works well threading through other perennials without overwhelming them. The airy white flowers brighten shaded and partly shaded borders where darker-flowered geraniums can look heavy, and shearing the foliage back after bloom keeps the clump fresh through the rest of the season. Divide every three to four years to maintain vigor and control spread.
